p3 has a light-blue monopoly with hotels and owns the brown set. The current offer from p1 would give up $100 and Park Place for two mortgaged properties. I rejected similar trades earlier because they would leave me unable to cover hotel costs on my yellow monopoly.

Recalling exact mortgage values to check if the trade is feasible. St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue each mortgage for $90, so unmortgaging them would cost $99 each. New York mortgages for $100. Park Place mortgages for $175. Atlantic Avenue mortgages for $130.

Unmortgaging both orange properties would cost $198. That leaves only $311 after the trade, which is too little to cover a light-blue hotel without mortgaging my yellow monopoly. If I keep them mortgaged instead, I have $639 in cash and mortgage value, enough for the hotel without breaking yellow. The downside is that I cannot collect rent or build on those orange properties until they are unmortgaged.

I already have enough cash and mortgage buffers to cover a light-blue hotel without the trade. Park Place would be lost as a $175 buffer. The yellow monopoly is preferable to an undeveloped orange set.

The orange set is the best landed-on property, but I cannot safely unmortgage it yet without more cash. After the trade, p1 would have $148 and could not immediately unmortgage Boardwalk, which costs $220; they would need to mortgage their railroads instead.

Mortgaging all four railroads would leave p1 with only $328 after unmortgaging Boardwalk. That is not enough for one house on each dark blue property, since building evenly costs $400 total.

p1 cannot build dark blue immediately even with this trade. If they mortgage all four railroads to unmortgage Boardwalk, they would have only $328 after paying the $220 unmortgage cost, which is still below the $400 needed for one house on each property.
